subject: computer
source: CISCE Curriculum for Primary Classes I-V (2016), official

covers: Understand that a computer is a machine made by humans
Know that a computer does its work by following the inputs and instructions it is given
Tell a desktop from a laptop
Name some things a computer can do, such as play games and music or book tickets
Sort objects into natural things and man-made things
Name places where computers are used
List everyday uses: typing, music, games, the internet, email and chat
Know that computers store data and give information
Name the main parts: monitor, keyboard, mouse and CPU
Say what each main part does: input, processing and output
Name extra devices such as printer, scanner, microphone and speaker
Show how the parts are connected and work together
Keep the computer clean and handle it gently
Sit with the right posture and distance from the screen
Avoid touching connecting cords and wires, and never bang the computer
Share the computer, take turns, and never snatch a mouse or keyboard from a friend
Close the computer properly when turns are over
Keep the sound at a comfortable level
Name the left and right buttons and the scroll wheel
Use the left click, right click and scroll wheel
Know why a mouse pad helps the mouse move smoothly
Build hand control by practising with the mouse
Find the alphabet, number and arrow keys
Use keys to type text and move around
Know that the keyboard is mainly used to type text
Describe data in simple words
Name storage devices such as pen drive, data card, CD and DVD
Know that data can be stored for a short time or for a long time
